chapter: MJQ, Pettiford and the move to Paris
title: Recording with Sonny Rollins and a Blue Note altoist; rapport with Percy Heath
summary: They recorded a lot with Sonny Rollins and a young altoist whose name he can't recall; he and Percy Heath knew every tempo without counting off.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: So then we got Sonny Rollins, which we did a lot of recordings with Sonny, and we recorded quite a bit with another alto player, who was --
No. No. He was with -- he had the contract with Blue Note. So we began to record with him a lot.
It's right on the end of my tongue, like always.
Who was he working with before?
Oh, he was just a kind of a --
Yeah, just coming up, but very good, a very good alto player. Oh, we did a lot of records with him. I can't think of his name.
That wasn't Lucky Thompson, was it?
Oh, no. No, no. No, no. No, he was an alto player, a good alto player, too. Oh, why can't I think of his name?

Then, this was around '52, '51, the latter part of '51, as I started right into working, you know, trying to get things done as quickly as I could. And well, we did quite a few things, you know, at Town Hall, with J.J., and things like that.
And we got so tight together that Percy and I, any tune you'd call, we could start off playing without stomping off. We just knew all the tempos.
And we had such an understanding, it was fantastic.
